content:
# Disagreement Log — 1 Maccabees Chapter 5

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Translators:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 36

---

## Disagreement Entries

**1MA 5:1 — "greatly enraged" vs. "exceedingly angry" vs. "furious"**
- EMET: "they were exceedingly angry"
- LOGOS: "they were greatly enraged"
- PNEUMA: "they were furious"
- RULING: "they were greatly enraged" — LOGOS; "enraged" captures *orgisthesan sphodra* well; "furious" (PNEUMA) is too casual

**1MA 5:2 — "race of Jacob" vs. "descendants of Jacob"**
- EMET: "race of Jacob"
- LOGOS: "descendants of Jacob"
- PNEUMA: "descendants of Jacob"
- RULING: "descendants of Jacob" — *genos Iakob* = the people/lineage; "race" has modern connotations to avoid

**1MA 5:3 — "sons of Esau in Idumea" vs. "Idumeans in Akrabattene"**
- EMET: "sons of Esau in Idumea"
- LOGOS: "Idumeans in Akrabattene"
- PNEUMA: "Idumeans at Akrabattene"
- RULING: "Idumeans in Akrabattene" — LOGOS; the text specifies Akrabattene as the location; "sons of Esau" is preserved in v.65 context (Hebron) but here Akrabattene is the named place

**1MA 5:3 — "humbled them" — all agree**
- No disagreement.

**1MA 5:4 — "wickedness" vs. "malice" vs. (not separately rendered)**
- EMET: "wickedness of the sons of Baean"
- LOGOS: "malice of the sons of Baean"
- RULING: "malice of the sons of Baean" — *kakian* = malice/wickedness; LOGOS's "malice" is more targeted

**1MA 5:5 — "utterly devoted them to destruction" vs. "put them under the ban"**
- EMET: "utterly devoted them to destruction"
- LOGOS: "put them under the ban"
- PNEUMA: "put them under the ban"
- RULING: "put them under the ban of destruction" — combining both; the *herem* (Greek *anethematisen*) requires both the ritual language "ban" and the functional "destruction"

**1MA 5:6 — "might force and much people" vs. "large and powerful force"**
- EMET: "mighty force and much people"
- LOGOS: "large and powerful force"
- PNEUMA: "large, strong force"
- RULING: "large and powerful force" — LOGOS; "much people" is archaic

**1MA 5:8 — "turned back to Judea" vs. "headed back toward Judea"**
- Minor variation. "Turned back toward Judea" preferred.

**1MA 5:9 — "stronghold of Dathema" — all agree**
- The place name Dathema is preserved by all translators. No disagreement.

**1MA 5:10-13 — The letter from Gilead — general tone**
- EMET: More formal, epistolary tone
- LOGOS: Clear and direct
- PNEUMA: Terse, urgent
- RULING: LOGOS formulation preserved for the letter; it maintains the urgent-but-measured tone of the original

**1MA 5:13 — "about a thousand souls"**
- All agree. "About a thousand souls" or "about a thousand people." LOGOS: "about a thousand people." Adopted.

**1MA 5:14 — "Galilee of the Foreigners" vs. "all the Galilee of the Gentiles"**
- EMET: "Galilee of the Foreigners"
- LOGOS: "Galilee of the Gentiles"
- PNEUMA: (simply "every Gentile in Galilee")
- RULING: "all the Galilee of the Gentiles" — this is the standard designation found in Isaiah 9:1 (LXX) and echoed here deliberately; "of the Gentiles" is the established rendering

**1MA 5:17 — "I and Jonathan my brother" vs. "My brother Jonathan and I"**
- EMET: "I and Jonathan my brother"
- LOGOS: "My brother Jonathan and I"
- RULING: "My brother Jonathan and I" — more natural English word order; no loss of meaning

**1MA 5:20 — "Three thousand men were assigned to Simon" — all agree on the numbers**
- No disagreement.

**1MA 5:22 — "to the gate of Ptolemais" vs. "to the very gate of Ptolemais"**
- EMET: "to the gate of Ptolemais"
- LOGOS: "to the very gate of Ptolemais"
- PNEUMA: "to the very gates of Ptolemais"
- RULING: "to the very gate of Ptolemais" — LOGOS; the *heos* (all the way to) justifies "very gate"

**1MA 5:23 — "and all that they had" vs. "everything they had" vs. "everything they owned"**
- Minor variation. "All that they had" or "all their possessions." LOGOS "everything they possessed" adopted.

**1MA 5:24 — "three days' journey in the wilderness"**
- All agree. No disagreement.

**1MA 5:25 — "received him peaceably" vs. "welcomed them peaceably"**
- EMET: "received him peaceably"
- LOGOS: "welcomed them peaceably"
- PNEUMA: "greeted them peacefully"
- RULING: "welcomed them peaceably" — LOGOS; the plural "them" is correct (Judas and Jonathan)

**1MA 5:28 — "struck Bosora in the way" vs. "struck Bosora through the desert road"**
- EMET: "struck Bosora in the way"
- LOGOS: "marched by the desert road to Bosora"
- RULING: "struck Bosora through the desert road" — the approach route through the desert is significant tactically

**1MA 5:30 — "beyond numbering" vs. "an enormous force"**
- EMET: "beyond numbering"
- LOGOS: "beyond counting"
- PNEUMA: "couldn't even be counted"
- RULING: "beyond counting" — LOGOS; more natural English

**1MA 5:32 — "Fight today for your brothers" vs. "Fight today for your kindred"**
- EMET/PNEUMA: "brothers"
- LOGOS: "kindred"
- RULING: "Fight today for your kindred!" — *adelphous* is literally "brothers" but LOGOS's "kindred" is inclusive and appropriate for a mixed community; however, in a battlefield exhortation, "brothers" has more force. RULING: "Fight today for your brothers!"

**1MA 5:33 — "cried in prayer" vs. "crying out in prayer"**
- Minor variation. "Crying out in prayer" (LOGOS) preferred.

**1MA 5:35 — "turned aside to Maspha" vs. "wheeled against Maspha"**
- EMET: "turned aside to Maspha"
- LOGOS: "wheeled against Maspha"
- PNEUMA: "swung south to Maspha"
- RULING: "turned against Maspha" — preserves the military turn without directional inference not in the text

**1MA 5:37 — "beyond the stream" vs. "on the far side of the ravine"**
- EMET: "beyond the stream"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "on the far side of the ravine"
- RULING: "on the far side of the ravine" — *cheimarrou* = winter stream / ravine; LOGOS/PNEUMA capture the defensive significance better

**1MA 5:42 — "scribes of the people" vs. "officers of the army"**
- EMET: "scribes of the people" (very literal: *grammateis tou laou*)
- LOGOS: "officers of the army"
- PNEUMA: "officers"
- RULING: "officers of the army" — *grammateis* in this military context are adjutants/officers; "scribes" misleads

**1MA 5:43 — "temple precinct in Carnaim" vs. "temple precinct at Carnaim"**
- Minor variation. "Temple precinct at Carnaim" preferred.

**1MA 5:45 — "from small to great" vs. "young and old"**
- EMET: "from small to great" (literal)
- LOGOS: "young and old"
- PNEUMA: "old and young"
- RULING: "young and old" — the Greek *apo mikrou heos megalou* is an idiom for "everyone"; "young and old" is the standard English equivalent

**1MA 5:46 — "no way to turn from it on the right hand or on the left"**
- EMET: "no way to turn from it on the right hand or on the left"
- LOGOS: "no way to bypass it, either right or left"
- RULING: "no way to bypass it, to the right or the left" — LOGOS; "right hand or left" is more archaic

**1MA 5:47 — "blocked the gates with stones"**
- All agree. No disagreement.

**1MA 5:51 — "passed through the city over the slain"**
- All agree on this striking detail. No disagreement.

**1MA 5:53 — "gathering the stragglers and encouraging the people"**
- All agree on substance. LOGOS formulation adopted.

**1MA 5:60 — "borders of Judea" — all agree**
- No disagreement.

**1MA 5:61 — "thinking to do bravely" vs. "had gone out on their own initiative" vs. "charged out on their own"**
- EMET: "thinking to do bravely"
- LOGOS: "had gone out on their own initiative"
- PNEUMA: "charged out on their own"
- RULING: "had gone out on their own initiative" — LOGOS; the issue is unauthorized action, not mistaken courage

**1MA 5:62 — "seed of the men" vs. "stock of those men"**
- EMET: "seed of the men through whose hands salvation had been given"
- LOGOS: "stock of those men through whose hands deliverance had been given"
- PNEUMA: "family of men through whose hands Israel had been saved"
- RULING: "stock of those men through whose hands deliverance had been given to Israel" — LOGOS; "stock" preserves the genealogical/typological claim; "deliverance" over "salvation" is appropriate here (military context)

**1MA 5:67 — "desiring to do bravely" vs. "eager to win honor" vs. "wanted to win glory"**
- EMET: "desiring to do bravely"
- LOGOS: "eager to win honor"
- PNEUMA: "wanted to win glory and gone out to fight without any order"
- RULING: "eager to win honor" — LOGOS; they were motivated by personal ambition for honor (*philotimia*) rather than genuine zeal; "without authorization" captures the critical parallel to vv.61-62

**1MA 5:68 — "carved images of their gods" — all agree**
- All translators preserve "carved images." No disagreement.
